(Per Hon'ble Sri Justice Tarlada Rajasekhar Rao) The present appeal is registered under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act 1894 (for short referred to as "Act") on the reference made under Section 18 of the Act aggrieved by the Judgment and Decree dated 12.12.2007 on the file of the Principal Senior Civil Judge at Kakinada in fixing the compensation at the rate of Rs.2,00,000/- qua the prevailing rate of Rs 4,00,000/- per acre, where the acquisition department has acquired the land belongs to the appellant (herein after called as "claimant") before the Reference Court for the purpose of expansion of Industrial Area for A.P.I.I.C. Limited in an extent of Ac.3.93 cents in Sy.
No.124/2 situated in Jaggammagaripeta village.
And the APIIC has filed cross-objection vide 9811 of 2010.
2. The land acquisition department has issued 4(1) Notification under the Act on 08.03.1999 and the possession was taken on 15.06.2001.
Award No.1/2000 was delivered on 20.08.2000.

The land was acquired for the purpose of expansion of Industrial area in Jaggammagaripeta village and the compensation was fixed at Rs.1,30,000/- per acre as the LAO has found that lands are not fertile lands, no irrigation sources to the acquired land and the soil is reddish with gravel, and no structures.
But the LAO observed some mango, neem, palmyra, teak tree are available here and there in the acquisition land.
3. Aggrieved by the fixation of land at the rate of Rs.1,30,000/- per acre, the claimant has requested the LAO to refer the issue under Section 18 of the Act.

The Reference Court has fixed the compensation at the rate of Rs.2,00,000/- per acre relying on the sale statistics and relying on the value of the land in Sy No.89/1 for an extent of Ac.1-62 cents appears to be the proximate land,
discarding the value of other lands referred by the LAO by deducting 1/3rd of the land towards development of agricultural land into industrial use.
4. Now aggrieved by the fixation of the land value at the rate of Rs.2,00,000/- per acre, the present Appeal.
The Claimant he himself was examined as PW1.

In the chief examination it was depicted that the acquired land is at the distance of 2 furlongs from 100 feet A.D.B. Road and it is situated in between the B.S.E.S. Power Station and Food Corporation Godowns and a road is also situated, a school building and other residential and non-residential buildings situated near and adjoining.

And it is further stated that PW-2 and his family member have sold the lands to B.S.E.S. Andhra Power Ltd vide Ex. R-1 to R-5 at the rate of Rs.3,15,000/- per acre in Sy.No 86/1 of Jaggammagaripeta village and acquired lands worth of Rs.7,00,000/- per acre, hence, prayed to enhance the compensation to Rs.4,00,000/- per acre with all consequential benefits under the Act.
The counsel for the Claimant has relied on the judgments Satish and others Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and others1 and Horrmal since deceased through his LR's Vs. State of Haryana and others.2 5.

Both PW-1 (claimant) and PW-2 in the testimonies of their cross-examination, were not able to withstand as stated in their chief examination and further stated that lands purchased under Ex. P2 to P5 were situated in Bhimavaram village and the land under acquisition is situated in Jaggammagaripeta village, and admittedly the lands are far away from the land acquired under the Ex P-2 to P-5.
And admitted that the lands under acquisition are not situated in between the B.S.E.S. Power Station and Food Corporation Godowns as deposed in the chief affidavit.

8. R.W-1 the Special Deputy Tahsildar Land Acquisition Unit for APIIC Limited has deposed that earlier to the award 1/2000 land was acquired under award No-4/1998 which is consent award and the land owners agreed to receive an amount of Rs.2,00,000/- per acre including all the statutory payments like solatium, additional market value, interest etc., and the said fact was mentioned in the award No-1 / 2000 and the land under Ex. P-1 to P-5 is having special advantage and special necessity for that land and therefore they paid more than the prevailing market rate for the land.
9. R.W-1 the Special Deputy Tahsildar Land Acquisition Unit for APIIC Limited has stated in the testimony of her cross- examination that she has no idea of topography of the acquired land and has no personal knowledge about RW-1 document and further stated the lands will be registered as per Basic Value Register.
10.

entities.text: Special Deputy Tahsildar Land Acquisition Unit
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: The counsel for beneficiary department Sri Gurram Ramachandra Rao has emphasised his argument on the sole ground that the Reference Court erred in granting interest from the date of Section 4(1) Notification (8.3.1999) as against the date of taking possession (15.06.2001), which is not in-consonance with the statutory provisions as adumbrated in Sections 28 & 34 of the Act and the grant of interest on compensation is payable from the date of taking possession of the land under the provisions of the Act.
He relied on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Subh Ram and others Vs. State of Haryana and another3.

entities.text: Subh Ram and others Vs. State of Haryana and another3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The judgment has no relevance to the contention raised by the beneficiary department.

The possession was taken on 15.06.2001 and the date of notification is 08.03.1999.
11.

Section 28 of the Land Acquisition Act envisages that if the Court grants more money than the Collector has given as (2010) 1 SCC 444 compensation, the Collector may be ordered to pay interest on the excess rate starting on the date on which he took possession.

12. On perusal of the documents filed by the Claimant and the testimonies of the PW-1 and PW-2 and the testimony of RW-1 and examining the arguments advanced by the respective counsel, the point for consideration is whether the Reference Court has answered the reference in accordance with law and fixed the fair market value?
13. On perusal of the evidence and of PW-1 and PW-2 and Ex. R-1, the land in Sy.No-89/1 and 86/1 and the land under acquisition of the Claimant in Sy.No.124/1 belongs to Jaggammagaripeta village.

sentences.text: PW-2 sold the land at the rate of Rs.3,00,000/- per acre and RW-1 has not specifically denied the land value of Ex P-1 in his chief examination and the LAO has not inspected the land under acquisition physically.
14. The judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Subh Ram and others Vs. State of Haryana and another4 is not much assistance to the Claimant.

entities.text: Subh Ram and others Vs. State of Haryana and another4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Punjab & Haryana High Court has relied on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Mehrawal Khawaja (2010) 1 SCC 444 Trust Vs. State of Punjab5 wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has ruled that "When the land is being compulsorily taken away from a person, he is entitled to the highest value which similar land in the locality is shown to have fetched in a bonafide transaction entered into between a willing purchaser and a willing seller near about the time of the acquisition.
15. Admittedly the land in Sy. No.89/1 and the land under acquisition under Sy.No.124/1 are situated in same village and is at the distance of less than 1 KM and the lands that are acquired under award No. 4/1998 are bonafide transaction and as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Mehrawal Khawaja Trust Vs. State of Punjab6 if the lands are in similar land in the same locality and near about the time, acquisition can be considered as bonafide transaction.

entities.text: Mehrawal Khawaja (2010) 1 SCC 444 Trust Vs. State of Punjab5
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Mehrawal Khawaja Trust Vs. State of Punjab6
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Undoubtedly, the lands are in the similar land and in the same locality of Jaggamagaripeta village.

Hence, without hesitation, we take the land value of Ex. P-2 as a basis for the fixation of the compensation of the land under acquisition of the Claimant in an extent of Ac.3.92 cents in Sy. No.124/1 and fix the compensation as Rs.3,00,000/- (in words three lakhs) per acre.
However, 1/5th has to be deducted towards development charges as the acquisition is for the expansion of the industrial area.
16. The Reference Court has awarded interest under Section 28 of the Act from the date of notification i.e., 08.03.1999 instead of date of taking possession i.e., 15.06.2001.
Hence, the Claimant is entitled interest as per Section 28 of the Act from the date of taking possession.
The issue is answered in favour the X-objector.

17. Accordingly the Appeal is disposed of fixing the compensation at the rate of Rs.3,00,000/-
(Rupees three lakhs only) per acre and the Claimant is entitled to all the statutory benefits under the Land Acquisition Act 1894,
1/5th of the land value shall be deducted towards development charges as the land acquisition is for the expansion of the industrial area.
In view of the discussion in paragraph No.16, I.A.No.2 of 2010(X-Obj.9811/2010) is disposed of.
However both parties shall bear their own costs.
As a sequel, interlocutory applications, if any pending in these appeals shall stand dismissed.
